verified_by: 3-state differential (direct javac + java, JDK 11) on the real production YamlMap loading path. NOT run through 02_verify_bbc.py: the project builds with Gradle and the verifier drives Maven only, so the three states were compiled and run by hand.
note: FIRST VERIFIED CASE OUTSIDE XSTREAM. Found by asking whether a behavioural break can hide UNDERNEATH a syntactic one: snakeyaml was already in the catalog and had been mined to a zero, but every search term in that entry targeted the TAG/DESERIALIZATION break (SafeConstructor, TagInspector, CVE-2022-1471), whose adaptations are constructor-arity fixes forced by javac. The RESOURCE LIMITS are a separate behavioural break in the same library, introduced at a different boundary (1.32), and nobody had searched for them. This case is the two-step pattern in the wild: the client fixed the compile error in an earlier commit, shipped, then hit the runtime limit against real data and fixed that separately.
discovery_method: Scanned the snakeyaml compile-break-classified candidates for a SEMANTIC edit alongside the syntactic one (1 of 9 had one). Then confirmed a population existed before mining: 41 client commits across setCodePointLimit (15), setMaxAliasesForCollections (16), setAllowDuplicateKeys (10).

discovery._why_explicit: census.py falls back to _infer_break, which maps artifact_id 'snakeyaml' to snakeyaml-1.x-to-2.0-safeconstructor. There are now TWO snakeyaml breaks in the catalog and this case belongs to the resource-limit one, so the attribution must be stated rather than inferred — otherwise the census credits it to the break it was NOT found under.

library.breaking_boundary: 1.32 (3 MB code-point limit imposed by default)

in_repo_version_transition.mechanism: direct bump of snakeYamlVersion in gradle.properties
in_repo_version_transition.evidence: Walking the history of gradle.properties gives the whole version timeline: 1.30 -> 1.31 (2022-06), 1.31 -> 1.32 @68d44a35 (2022-09-15), 1.32 -> 1.33 (2022-10), 1.33 -> 2.0 (2022-12). Verified directly rather than inferred: gradle.properties at 68d44a35's parent reads 1.31, and at 68d44a35 reads 1.32. `compare` confirms 68d44a35 is an ANCESTOR of the adaptation, 22 commits before it.
in_repo_version_transition.elapsed: almost exactly two years — bumped 2022-09-15, adapted 2024-09-04
in_repo_version_transition.note_on_versions: By the adaptation commit the project had moved on to snakeyaml 2.0, so the adaptation's own parent is on 2.0, not 1.32. The break was introduced at 1.32 and carried forward; the crossing that matters is the 1.31 -> 1.32 bump above.
in_repo_version_transition.why_the_pipeline_dropped_it: THE VERSION IS NOT IN A BUILD FILE THE PIPELINE READS. bbc_e2e's traversal walks pom.xml / build.gradle, but this project declares snakeYamlVersion in gradle.properties and interpolates it (`yaml "org.yaml:snakeyaml:$snakeYamlVersion"`). So find_boundary_bump saw no version anywhere and reported 'no boundary-crossing DIRECT-dep bump', and the `mvn dependency:tree` recheck could not help either because the project is Gradle. The crossing was there the whole time, 22 commits back, and a human found it in one pass over the file's history. This is a fixable gap, not a property of the client.

bump_source: snakeyaml 1.32 release; the limit is documented as DoS hardening (CVE-2022-38749..38752 family).

behavioral_break.mechanism: snakeyaml 1.32 imposes a 3 MB (3145728 code point) ceiling on incoming documents BY DEFAULT, and adds LoaderOptions.setCodePointLimit to raise it. A client that constructs a plain Yaml and loads a document larger than 3 MB parsed fine before the boundary and throws after it. No signature changed on the client's path, so the client compiles unchanged and fails at run time.
behavioral_break.observed_exception: org.yaml.snakeyaml.error.YAMLException: The incoming YAML document exceeds the limit: 3145728 code points.
behavioral_break.blast_radius: Only clients loading YAML larger than 3 MB. Measured, not assumed: a 2 MB document parses identically on both sides of the boundary.

adaptation.repo_note: OpenText InfoArchive SIP SDK. Multi-module Gradle; the `yaml` module wraps snakeyaml behind YamlMap.
adaptation.commit_message: Minor release for 12.8.4 to Increase codePointLimit of LoaderOptions in Snakeyaml
adaptation.purity: The parent commit ALREADY contained `new SafeConstructor(new LoaderOptions())`, so the constructor-arity compile break had been fixed earlier. This commit contains no syntactic repair at all — it is a pure behavioural adaptation, which is what makes it evidence for the hidden-behind-a-compile-break hypothesis.

verification.method: 3-state differential over the client's real production entry point, YamlMap.from(String). Only the `core` package of the `yaml` module was compiled (javac, JDK 11) against snakeyaml plus commons-io 2.11.0, evo-inflector 1.3 and jsr305 3.0.2 — the project's own Gradle build was not used, because the verifier drives Maven and a full Gradle build was unnecessary to isolate this path.
verification.test: Driver.java (authored). Builds a single YAML scalar of N MB and calls YamlMap.from(String). Authored because the project has no >3 MB fixture — nobody checks one into a repository, which is precisely why this break only ever showed up against production data.

states.name: 2_broken
states.result: THREW org.yaml.snakeyaml.error.YAMLException: The incoming YAML document exceeds the limit: 3145728 code points.

verification.isolation: States 2 and 3 use the SAME snakeyaml jar (2.0). The only variable between them is the client's own commit, which isolates the adaptation as the cause of recovery. States 1 and 2 use the same client code, which isolates the library version as the cause of the break.
threats_to_validity: THE BASELINE IS A STAND-IN, but the crossing is now LOCATED. The client bumped 1.31 -> 1.32 at 68d44a35 (2022-09-15) and adapted 22 commits / two years later, by which time they were on 2.0. So state 1 (snakeyaml 1.31) reproduces the version they were actually on BEFORE the boundary, though not the version at the adaptation's immediate parent. The mechanism and the crossing are both established; what is reconstructed is the pairing of the two.
THE TEST IS AUTHORED, not the client's. Their suite has no >3 MB fixture. The code under test is entirely theirs; only the trigger is ours.

THE BUILD IS PARTIAL. Only the `core` package was compiled, not the whole Gradle project. That is sufficient for this path (YamlMap has no further intra-project dependencies) but it is not the project's own build.

scope.why: The pipeline discarded this case TWICE, for two independent reasons, and neither is a property of the client. (1) verifiable=False because build_system != maven: 02_verify_bbc.py drives Maven, so Gradle projects are written off before any harness is attempted. (2) The traversal found no bump because the version lives in gradle.properties, which it does not read. It was found and verified BY HAND.
scope.reproducible_by: scratchpad/snakeyaml-infoarchive-harness/run_differential.sh — direct javac/java, NOT 02_verify_bbc.py and NOT the project's own Gradle build.
scope.precedent: xstream-tvrenamer is also a Gradle project, verified through a hand-built Maven harness. This is the second Gradle case in the set.
scope.implication: Marking every Gradle project 'not verifiable' removes a large share of the Java population from the study BEFORE asking whether it broke. Combined with the gradle.properties blind spot, some part of the measured rarity is tooling reach rather than the phenomenon.
